kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore nature in Argentina, Peru and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Nature experiences on Ada Tours itineraries through Argentina, Peru and Uruguay are not evenly distributed. Argentina offers Iguazu Falls, Peru has high-altitude Lake Titicaca and Machu Picchu, while Uruguay is represented by a short trip across the Río de la Plata to Montevideo. These three countries are a subset of longer six- and eight-country tours, rather than a separate nature expedition across just three countries.
---

## Argentina, Peru and Uruguay: where nature really features

**In this combination, the main nature-focused days are at Iguazu in Argentina and in the Andes in Peru.** The current Uruguay sections introduce travelers to Montevideo and the Río de la Plata waterfront, but do not include an independent excursion to the country's national parks.

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The catalog includes a [20-day journey through six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and a [32-day route through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Both visit Argentina, Peru and Uruguay, but their overall geographical scope is considerably broader. Selecting this intersection does not mean there is a separate tour confined to those three countries.

The [general Argentina + Peru + Uruguay catalog](/multi-country/argentina_peru_uruguay/) shows the same geographical combination without the thematic filter. Here, the priority is to compare the actual nature experiences.

## Argentina: both sides of Iguazu within the full itinerary

On both journeys, the group arrives in the [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) area after visiting the Brazilian side of the falls. Exploring the Argentine side allows travelers to walk along the boardwalks near the cascades and approach [Devil's Throat](/argentina/place/garganta-del-diablo/).

For the nature theme, this is **the main stop in Argentina**. The rest of the country's program focuses on Buenos Aires, with city excursions and tango culture. It does not include a separate multi-day trip to Patagonia or Argentina's glaciers.

Some boardwalks at Iguazu may be restricted when water levels rise. For example, Argentina's National Parks Administration reported the temporary removal of walkways to Devil's Throat in 2026 for visitor safety. It is therefore important to check which routes are open before departure, rather than promise permanent access to every viewpoint.

## Uruguay: one day in Montevideo, not a nature expedition

The [20-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) includes a ferry journey from Buenos Aires across the Río de la Plata to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), with a city excursion and return trip. The [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) likewise includes a one-day visit to Montevideo.

Uruguay's contribution to the nature experience on these tours is therefore mainly **the scenery of the broad estuary during the ferry crossing**. The day itself focuses on the city rather than extended wildlife watching, a marine safari or excursions to Uruguayan nature parks. This is an important limitation for travelers who want to explore nature in every country on their itinerary.

If Uruguay's natural areas are a priority, compare specific itineraries that explicitly include them rather than assuming they are covered simply because the country appears on the route.

## Peru: Lake Titicaca, the Andes and Machu Picchu

Peru offers a different kind of nature: great altitude and mountain scenery. Both itineraries include high-altitude [Lake Titicaca and Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), the journey to Cusco and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Altitude, temperature and transfer times vary along the way.

Machu Picchu is first and foremost an Inca historical monument, but its natural setting of steep green slopes is a reason to visit in its own right. It is important to distinguish a sightseeing visit to the complex from a full multi-day trek. These itineraries describe an excursion to Machu Picchu, not a separate ascent along a challenging mountain route.

The high-altitude section calls for preparation. Following flights and the journey onward from Argentina, travelers should consider gradual ascent, rest and their individual well-being. Even if Peru is only one part of a larger tour, it cannot be planned like an ordinary city day at sea level.

| Country | Nature experiences on the current tours |
|---|---|
| Argentina | [Iguazu Falls](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) |
| Uruguay | [Río de la Plata and Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) |
| Peru | [Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) |

## 20 or 32 days: what changes when you choose

The [20-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) focuses on Brazil, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, a short visit to Uruguay, followed by Chile, Bolivia and Peru. Its overall geography is more compact, but it is still not a journey limited to the three selected countries.

The [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) continues beyond Peru to Ecuador, the Galápagos Islands and Colombia. Those additional nature experiences belong to **other countries**, so it would be wrong to count the Galápagos among the nature attractions of Argentina, Peru or Uruguay.

When comparing the options, consider the number of days at the waterfalls and in Peru, flight arrangements and opportunities for rest after high-altitude transfers. If your aim is to experience nature in all three selected countries, you will need an itinerary that includes separate nature stops in Uruguay.

## Preparation, seasons and borders

Conditions at the waterfalls are humid, and viewing walkways can be wet. Nights around Titicaca and Cusco are cooler, while sunshine at altitude is more intense. A rain jacket, comfortable footwear, sun protection and warm clothing for the Andes will be useful.

On these itineraries, Uruguay is reached by ferry from Argentina; flights and ground journeys through other countries follow. Travel documents and entry requirements should be checked **for the entire itinerary**, taking account of the traveler's citizenship and the return route.

Accommodation, transfer arrangements, guide languages and domestic flights differ between the tours. We help coordinate the logistics of the chosen itinerary, but inclusion in a nature-themed selection does not imply that every country has its own guided national park excursion.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a nature excursion in Uruguay?

On these tours, Uruguay is represented by a one-day trip to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). Separate visits to Uruguayan nature parks are not included.

### Can I see Iguazu and Machu Picchu on one trip?

Yes. Both attractions feature on the [20-day](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and [32-day](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) itineraries. The journey between them includes stops in other countries and high-altitude sections.

### Do I need to prepare for the altitude in Peru?

Yes. Titicaca and Cusco are considerably above sea level. Consider the pace of travel and your tolerance for exertion in advance, particularly if you have health concerns.

kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Wildlife and safaris: the full route through three countries"
lead: >-
  The wildlife and safari theme within the Argentina, Peru and Uruguay combination is represented by a 32-day tour through eight countries. In these three countries, the itinerary includes Iguazu Falls, Lake Titicaca, Andean landscapes and a city visit to Montevideo; the main wildlife-viewing opportunities, however, are in Bolivia and the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador. We explain which excursions are actually included and how the wildlife theme differs from the nature theme.
---

## Wildlife and safaris: where animals are observed on the full route

This selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} visiting [Argentina](/argentina/), [Peru](/peru/) and [Uruguay](/uruguay/) with the wildlife and safari label. The [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) carries this as an additional interest. **There is no dedicated safari in the three selected countries**: excursions focusing on birds and marine animals are included in other parts of the wider journey.

That is an important distinction in practice. In Argentina, travelers visit Iguazu Falls. In Peru, they see Lake Titicaca and the mountains along the road to Cusco. In Uruguay, the current itineraries devote a day to Montevideo, including the port, squares and old town. They do not include a special excursion to a Uruguayan nature reserve or a wildlife-watching outing.

| Country | What the itinerary includes |
|---|---|
| Argentina | Iguazu Falls and walks near the cascades |
| Peru | Titicaca, high-altitude roads and the Andes |
| Uruguay | Montevideo; no dedicated nature excursion |
| Outside the selected three | Bolivia: flamingos at Laguna Colorada; Ecuador: Galápagos marine wildlife |

This is no reason to leave Uruguay off a trip: a city day can offer a welcome contrast after several nature-focused stops. But it would be a mistake to choose this selection for wildlife watching **specifically in Uruguay**.

## Argentina: Iguazu Falls as the main nature highlight

Both the [20-day six-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and the [32-day eight-country route](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) include the Argentine side of Iguazu. Visitors can admire the cascades from boardwalks and viewpoints, approaching the water from different directions. The format and accessible sections depend on park regulations and actual trail conditions.

The two sides of the border must be distinguished. [Puerto Iguazú in Argentina](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and [Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) have different visitor routes. The 32-day itinerary includes both sides; the Brazilian section also lists the Bird Park. **The Bird Park is in Brazil**, so it cannot be counted among the Argentine activities.

Iguazu is a powerful nature experience, but a walk by the waterfalls is not itself a safari or a specialist birdwatching excursion. Encounters with wild animals in the park cannot be guaranteed and should not be described as an included product without separate confirmation.

## Peru: highland scenery without an invented safari

On both journeys, the Peru section begins after high-altitude stops in Bolivia. The itinerary passes through the [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) area, then heads toward [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) via La Raya Pass and several cultural stops. [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and Lima follow.

For nature enthusiasts, the main appeal is the transition from the high plateau to the green slopes around Machu Picchu. The itinerary, however, primarily describes the road, landscapes and archaeological excursions. It **does not include a special trip to look for rare birds or mammals** in Peru. Those wishing to see particular species need a different location, season and type of guiding.

Altitude also changes how travelers should prepare. The Titicaca area is approximately 3,800 meters above sea level, while Cusco is around 3,350 meters. Temperatures are cooler, the sun is more intense, and exertion feels different than at the waterfalls or coast. Overnight stops and gradual ascent become especially important if someone is considering removing intermediate stages in [Bolivia](/bolivia/) from a customized trip.

## Where the main wildlife encounters happen on the full journey

When comparing the two tours, the other countries should not be mentally removed. After Peru, the [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) visits **the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador**; this is the separate stage with specific island wildlife experiences. Other parts of the route also include natural parks and landscapes.

The [20-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) includes waterfalls and Bolivian lagoons too. But its main themes are culture and history, and nature; it does not carry the wildlife label. It should not be marketed as a safari simply because it includes national parks and scenic landscapes.

If observing animals is your main goal, compare [multi-country wildlife and safari itineraries](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/); there is a separate [nature selection](/multi-country/interests/nature/) for waterfalls, mountains and lakes. If you specifically want the three countries without Ecuador and Bolivia, discuss a new route with dedicated nature attractions, rather than adding imaginary excursions to already published tours.

## Coordinating climate, documents and timing

A convenient itinerary is determined by more than the location of national parks. Iguazu in Argentina is warm and humid; Montevideo and Buenos Aires have different conditions; and in the Peruvian Andes, temperatures can change sharply between day and evening. Packing for this combination should include rain and sun protection, light clothing for warmer areas, and insulating layers for the highlands.

On the current tours, Uruguay is visited by ferry from Buenos Aires, followed by a return to Argentina. Depending on citizenship, travelers must check whether **re-entry into Argentina** is permitted and what documents are required for the ferry. The onward journey to Peru passes through other countries and involves flights or overland crossings that cannot be eliminated just by shortening the destination list.

Ada Tours helps travelers compare the order of visits, number of border crossings and suitable pace, coordinate the required excursions and determine which wildlife experiences can actually be included. Entry, insurance and health requirements are assessed separately for each participant. Specific flights, new excursions and their prices are confirmed for the chosen itinerary.

For the overall logistics, see the [Argentina + Peru + Uruguay catalog](/multi-country/argentina_peru_uruguay/). For the cultural content of the same stops, consult the [three-country history selection](/multi-country/argentina_peru_uruguay/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife on the three-country route

### Can visitors see wildlife in each of the three countries on the existing tour?

No. The current descriptions make no such promise. Iguazu is the main natural attraction in Argentina; Peru offers highland landscapes; and the Uruguay visit focuses on Montevideo.

### Is the Iguazu Bird Park included in the Argentine excursion?

No. The Bird Park is on the Brazilian side and is offered on the 32-day tour **for an additional fee**. The Argentine Iguazu excursion is a separate visit to the waterfalls.

### Where is the strongest wildlife-viewing component of the 32-day itinerary?

A dedicated nature stage is scheduled in the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador. This is outside the three selected countries, so it would not automatically remain part of a shortened itinerary.

### Is the trip suitable for someone with no high-altitude experience?

The route requires an assessment of health and adaptation to altitude. The significant elevations around Titicaca and Cusco must be considered in advance; for customized itineraries, discuss acclimatization with a doctor and the travel organizer.

kind: multi_country_combination
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore travel in Argentina and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Argentina and Uruguay are conveniently connected across the Río de la Plata: from Buenos Aires, travelers can visit Montevideo for a day or continue through historic Colonia del Sacramento to the beaches of Punta del Este. The choice depends on how much time you want to spend in Uruguay, whether an oceanfront holiday is important, and how ferry travel fits with onward flights. Compare actual Ada Tours itineraries and plan documents, expenses and weather on both sides of the border in advance.
---

## Argentina and Uruguay: from a ferry day trip to a journey of its own

**The main question when choosing an Argentina and Uruguay tour is how many days to devote to Uruguay.** From [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), you can cross the Río de la Plata and return the same evening. But that allows only an overview of the capital or a short walk around Colonia. To experience [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) and [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) on one trip, you need more time.

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with both countries on the main itinerary. One important detail: current Ada Tours programs also include Brazil and, in some cases, Chile. Selecting Argentina and Uruguay in the filter means both are visited, but **does not promise an itinerary consisting of only two countries**.

| Travel style | What you experience |
|---|---|
| Uruguay in one day | Montevideo and a return to Argentina |
| Uruguay with overnight stays | Colonia, the capital and the Atlantic coast |
| A longer circuit | Uruguay together with Iguazu and Patagonia |

These three options can look similar when reduced to a list of countries, yet they differ greatly in experience and pace.

### What Ada Tours itineraries actually offer

The [“Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay in 13 Days” tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) includes Rio, Iguazu and Buenos Aires, followed by a ferry to Colonia del Sacramento, time in Montevideo and several days of beach relaxation in Punta del Este. This is worth considering when Uruguay should be a substantial part of the holiday.

On the [26-day journey through Argentina and Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), Montevideo is a day excursion from Buenos Aires, with a return the same day. The rest of the route focuses on northern Argentina, wine regions, lakes, glaciers and southern Patagonia. Here, the day in Uruguay complements a much longer trip rather than replacing a holiday in Uruguay itself.

The [four-country South America itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) also includes a day trip from Buenos Aires to Montevideo; other parts of the journey run through Argentina, Brazil and Chile. It differs from the 13-day tour that includes accommodation on Uruguay's coast.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_stolitsy_latinskoj_ameriki,tour_source_vsya_argentina,tour_source_tur_v_4_strany_yuzhnoj_ameriki}}

## Crossing the Río de la Plata without losing a day in transit

There are several ways to travel between Buenos Aires and Uruguay. **A ferry to Colonia del Sacramento** works well if you want to start with its historic streets and then continue overland to Montevideo. **A ferry service to Montevideo** is suitable for reaching the capital directly, although some operators' itineraries use a ferry to Colonia followed by a bus. The destination name alone does not tell you whether a transfer is involved.

Buquebus and Colonia Express offer different routes and combinations of water and land travel. Four details are especially important when choosing a ticket: the exact departure port, the arrival port, whether a bus section is included, and the check-in time required for border procedures. In Colonia Express's autumn 2026 timetable, the Buenos Aires–Colonia crossing is shown as approximately 1 hour 15 minutes **on board the vessel**. This does not include travel from the hotel, check-in, immigration formalities or a possible bus transfer.

For a day trip, returning that same evening is a crucial part of the plan. Late arrival at the terminal, a weather-related delay or an inconvenient return ferry can cut the excursion short. If an international flight follows, it is better to allow a sufficient buffer between transfers than to schedule the ferry immediately before departure.

In Buenos Aires, also distinguish between Ezeiza Airport (EZE) and Aeroparque (AEP): transferring between them requires crossing the city. The ferry port is a third logistical location, so a statement such as "fly out immediately after the Uruguay excursion" says little about feasibility without the terminal details.

## Colonia, Montevideo or Punta del Este

[Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) is ideal for a short historical excursion. Founded by the Portuguese in 1680, it retains low-rise houses, cobbled streets and a network of lanes unusual for Spanish colonial city planning. Its historic quarter is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Allow time to explore the old town separately from boarding the next form of transport.

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) reveals itself through Independence Square, the old town, markets and the long waterfront promenade known as the Rambla. A day tour can cover the main neighborhoods, but an overnight stay makes it easier to enjoy a relaxed evening and stop for local food. Do not mistake a city sightseeing tour for a visit to Uruguay's entire Atlantic coastline: reaching the beach resorts requires another journey from the capital.

[Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) is a choice for beaches and resort relaxation. Several days of Ada Tours' 13-day itinerary are devoted to this part of the trip. The resort is busier during the peak summer season, and accommodation and transport prices may differ from those in the off-season. If enjoying the ocean is your main goal, a few hours between ferries will not do it justice.

For geographical context, start with the [Uruguay page](/uruguay/) and compare these three destinations rather than trying to fit them all into one excursion.

## When to travel: summer on the coast and walks around the cities

Argentina and Uruguay are both in the Southern Hemisphere, but climate varies along the different itineraries. Around Buenos Aires, Colonia and Montevideo, **December through February** is summer, with potentially hot days and high humidity. This is the most obvious season for a beach holiday in Punta del Este, but accommodation demand is also higher. Heat may be more tiring during city walks than the cooler spring or autumn weather.

**March–April and October–November** are often convenient for combining architecture, walking and travel without a need to swim every day. In winter, from June through August, the Río de la Plata estuary can be windy and damp. Bring a windproof outer layer, especially for open ferry decks and waterfront promenades.

If Patagonia is added to the two countries, the season should not be chosen based on Montevideo's weather alone. [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) and southern Chile are much colder and windier than the Río de la Plata area. These itineraries require clothing for both summer cities and glacier visits, while domestic flights add to the logistical demands.

## Borders, visas, insurance and travel documents

**Argentina and Uruguay have separate immigration regimes.** The ferry crosses an international border even when the journey feels short. Travelers need documents entitling them to enter each country, and returning to Argentina involves another entry.

For Russian citizens traveling on ordinary international passports, short tourist visits to both countries are possible without obtaining a tourist visa in advance under the applicable arrangements. Uruguay's Ministry of the Interior explicitly lists Russia among visa-exempt passports and requires separate authorization for other purposes of travel or longer stays. Rules may differ for citizens of other countries, holders of special travel documents and travelers with unusual immigration status.

Before buying tickets, check passport validity, permitted length of stay, documents for minors, onward travel plans and carrier requirements. **Argentine immigration legislation**, following amendments in 2025, provides for a declaration of the purpose of entry and the possession of medical insurance. Travel insurance should cover the whole route, taking account of the countries actually visited, planned activities and health risks.

If Brazil or Chile is part of the journey, check those countries' visa and transit rules separately. Crossing the Río de la Plata does not replace the document preparations needed for every other border on a longer itinerary.

## Pesos, payment cards and your travel budget

Argentina uses the Argentine peso (**ARS**), while Uruguay uses the Uruguayan peso (**UYU**). Sharing the name "peso" does not mean the currencies have the same value. A tour budget in US dollars, a hotel invoice and a local price in pesos are different amounts; consider the currency and payment method for each expense.

When planning costs, separate ferry and bus fares, accommodation, meals and excursions. Tickets and transfers already included in your chosen Ada Tours itinerary should not be counted twice, but **inclusions vary from tour to tour**. For example, the 26-day itinerary explicitly includes ferry tickets for the day excursion to Montevideo. Check the conditions on the pages of other tours.

Do not assume a payment card from any bank will work without difficulty: international acceptance depends on the issuing bank and payment infrastructure. Visa and Mastercard cards issued by Russian banks are not processed abroad through those payment networks. For daily expenses, it is wise to have a permitted cashless payment option and a modest cash reserve in an appropriate currency.

## Frequently asked questions about tours to Argentina and Uruguay

### Can I visit Uruguay from Buenos Aires without staying overnight?

Yes. The current [26-day tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) and [four-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) include a day excursion to Montevideo with a return to Buenos Aires. A visit to Colonia or an independent walk around the capital can also be arranged as a day trip, but the time needed for border formalities and the return ferry must be considered.

### Is there an itinerary with several nights in Uruguay?

Yes. The [13-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) passes through Colonia and Montevideo before allowing time for Punta del Este. This is a different experience from a one-day ferry excursion.

### Is passport control required on the ferry?

Yes. This is international travel. Procedures may take place at departure and arrival terminals according to the rules of the particular route. Do not plan solely around the sailing time.

### Which currency will I need after the ferry?

In Uruguay, expenses in the local currency are denominated in UYU; in Argentina, in ARS. For a short excursion, check what the tour includes first and plan the remaining spending around available payment and currency-exchange options.

### Which is better: a day excursion or several days in Uruguay?

Choose a day excursion for an introduction to the capital as part of a larger Argentina trip. Several days make more sense if you want to explore Colonia at leisure, discover Montevideo and relax on Punta del Este's coast.

## Argentina and Uruguay: finding adventure in the actual itinerary

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. All feature [Argentina and Uruguay](/multi-country/argentina_uruguay/) as main countries, but also travel through other parts of South America. The selected pair therefore should not automatically be presented as a standalone two-country journey offering trekking on both sides of the border.

In Argentina, the activities depend on the particular itinerary. [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) offers walks on designated paths above the waterfalls, while [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) features city excursions. The extensive [26-day Argentina and Patagonia itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) additionally reaches the mountain trails around El Chaltén and includes an off-road excursion in Tierra del Fuego.

The Uruguay section of these itineraries centers on [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/): a ferry crossing from Buenos Aires over the Río de la Plata, sightseeing in the capital and a return journey. **The adventure theme applies to the entire tour; it is not a promise of kayaking, hiking or a safari in Uruguay.** For travelers, this is a crucial distinction between the countries on a route and the activities actually included.

## Three distinct travel styles in one selection

**If trekking is your priority,** consider the [26-day Argentina and Patagonia route](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/). It includes a free day for independent hikes around [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/); the following day offers another opportunity for independent hiking or kayaking at an additional cost. The route also visits [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/), the glacial region around El Calafate and [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/). Free time for a trail does not mean a guided mountain trek is included in the price: the difficulty and conditions of the particular route need to be assessed separately.

**If you want to explore several countries in a limited time,** the [20-day six-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) includes Rio, both sides of Iguazu, Buenos Aires and a visit to Montevideo, before continuing through Chile, Bolivia and Peru. The days in Argentina focus on sightseeing; the most demanding sections in terms of altitude and road travel are outside Argentina and Uruguay.

**If you want the broadest possible geographical scope,** the [32-day eight-country journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also connects Argentina and Uruguay but continues as far as Ecuador and Colombia. It is a long sequence of city tours, nature stops, flights and ground transfers; its length alone does not prove that a challenging sporting trek is included.

Compare the current itineraries by their duration and contents:

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_vsya_argentina,tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## The Montevideo ferry crossing changes the travel plan

On the current itineraries, Buenos Aires and Montevideo are connected by ferry. This is a separate international border crossing even when the group returns to the Argentine capital on the same day. Travel documents, the departure port, terminal arrival time and the onward journey to the next stop must all be coordinated. Current schedules and entry conditions should be checked for the specific day and traveler's citizenship.

A one-day visit to Montevideo offers the historic center, Independence Square, the port and a walk around the city. This is not a beach expedition or several days of outdoor activities. If you want multiple adventure days in Uruguay, a customized route should be discussed separately; the itineraries shown here do not promise them.

For choosing Argentine activities independently, see [adventure tours in Argentina](/interests/adventure/tours/argentina/), and for a broader comparison of international routes, explore [multi-country adventure journeys](/multi-country/interests/adventure/).

## Preparing for Patagonia and a long journey

The physical demands of El Chaltén's trails are very different from a walk around Montevideo. Independent mountain hikes call for appropriate trekking shoes, protection from wind and rain, a supply of water and an understanding of the route's duration. Weather in Patagonia can change conditions rapidly even in the warmer months; a decision to set out is best based on the local forecast and the rules of the chosen trail.

Longer journeys also involve less obvious challenges: recovery days after flights, changing temperatures between subtropical waterfalls, Patagonia and highlands, baggage handling, connections and borders. It is worth planning payment options for both the Argentine and Uruguayan pesos in advance; card acceptance, currency exchange and cash withdrawals depend on the bank and route. We help coordinate the order of stops, connections and document-related questions for each journey.

If the trip is **primarily about active recreation**, begin by looking at how many actual days are allocated to trails, water-based activities or off-road travel. Then compare that with time spent on city visits and in transit. The two-country filter should not hide the fact that some of the adventures on these tours take place in other countries.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is trekking included in Uruguay on the existing tours?

No separate trekking program is confirmed for the Uruguay section of these itineraries. The included activities focus on Montevideo. Trekking opportunities in Argentine Patagonia are described separately in the [26-day tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/).

### Can I choose just Argentina and Uruguay without the other countries?

The tours shown here also include other main countries. A journey limited to these two would require a separately designed route and terms; the existing catalog does not promise such a two-country product.

### Where are the active activities most clearly defined?

Among the itineraries listed, the clearest destination for walking routes is [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) on the longer Argentina tour. However, those days are set aside for independent trekking, with kayaking offered as an optional activity. Check the specific trail and weather before deciding on a level of exertion.

### How can the ferry to Uruguay be combined with onward flights?

Allow sufficient time for passport procedures, travel from the terminal and the return to Buenos Aires. Connections should be planned around actual tickets and crossing times, not simply the geographical proximity of the two capitals.

## Argentina and Uruguay: culture and history on one journey

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Argentina and Uruguay among the main countries of the route and a focus on culture and history. This combination is especially interesting for comparing cities on opposite sides of the Río de la Plata. [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) reveals the history of Argentina's capital through its neighborhoods, monuments, theater and tango. In Uruguay, the historic center of [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) show other aspects of the colonial past and subsequent urban life.

**The amount of cultural sightseeing varies considerably.** The [13-day tour of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) devotes several consecutive days to the Argentine capital, a gaucho ranch and Uruguayan cities. On the [17-day four-country journey](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/), Uruguay is represented mainly by a one-day visit to Montevideo. A longer journey can include more countries while giving less time to a particular city.

To compare all tours involving these two countries, open the [Argentina + Uruguay catalog](/multi-country/argentina_uruguay/). You can also browse [cultural itineraries through Argentina](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/) and [cultural itineraries through Uruguay](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/uruguay/).

## Buenos Aires: from San Telmo to tango and gauchos

The 13-day journey through Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay includes a Buenos Aires city tour after Iguazu. Stops include San Telmo, La Boca, Recoleta, Puerto Madero, Teatro Colón and Plaza de Mayo. This day reveals different eras of the city: old streets, immigrant neighborhoods, historic-center architecture and newer waterfront districts.

San Telmo is known for its older streets and markets; [La Boca](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) is closely linked to the culture of the former port district, while Recoleta displays the capital's more formal architecture. Teatro Colón is among Argentina's foremost musical landmarks. Exploring with a guide who explains how these parts of Buenos Aires coexist helps put the city in context.

A separate day of the [13-day program](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) is devoted to the Don Silvano ranch outside the capital. Travelers experience gaucho traditions, horseback performances, music and an Argentine lunch. This is a cultural experience centered on the rural pampas, quite different from walking past architectural monuments in the city.

The [17-day route through Chile, Argentina, Uruguay and Brazil](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) includes Buenos Aires, a tango show and a ranch visit during its Argentine section. Several other days, however, focus on Patagonia, glaciers and Iguazu. Travelers interested in history and culture should look at the time actually allotted to Buenos Aires, rather than treat the entire tour duration as time spent exploring the capital's culture.

## Colonia del Sacramento: Portuguese streets on the Río de la Plata

[Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) stands out among Uruguayan cities for its preserved historic quarter, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Founded by the Portuguese in the 17th century, the town became one of the centers of rivalry between Portugal and Spain in the Río de la Plata region. Its winding stone streets and small-scale historic buildings evoke a past very different from the broad avenues of Buenos Aires.

On the [13-day tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/), the Uruguay section begins with a ferry from Buenos Aires to Colonia del Sacramento. A visit to the historic center is scheduled before the journey continues to Montevideo. Crossing the Río de la Plata becomes part of the story of the trip: within a short time, travelers arrive in a town with a different street plan and national traditions.

Not every tour through Argentina and Uruguay stops here. If Colonia is a must-see, **check that it appears in the day-by-day itinerary**. On some journeys, the ferry goes directly to Montevideo, with no separate visit to Colonia specified.

## Montevideo: Uruguay's capital, squares and everyday life

In [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), travelers discover Independence Square, Constitution Square, the cathedral and historic streets. Together they illustrate the city's development from a colonial port into a modern capital. Montevideo's architecture combines various European influences with local history, while its position beside the Río de la Plata shapes the waterfront and public spaces.

The 13-day journey includes an overnight stay and a Montevideo city tour after Colonia del Sacramento. It then continues to [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) for several days of beach relaxation. Thus, the Uruguay section includes both history and modern coastal life, although not every beach day is a cultural excursion.

The [17-day four-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) offers a very different format: Montevideo is a day trip by ferry from Buenos Aires, followed by a return to Argentina. There is enough time for a general introduction to the main streets and squares, but not for a leisurely journey through several Uruguayan cities.

The [32-day eight-country route](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also features a day excursion from Buenos Aires to Montevideo. The itinerary then continues to Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. Uruguay is an important stop, but only one part of a broad cultural and natural panorama of the continent.

## The Río de la Plata ferry and the logistics of a cultural itinerary

The ferry is an important planning element when combining Buenos Aires with Uruguay. Some itineraries travel to [Colonia del Sacramento](/uruguay/place/colonia-del-sacramento/) and continue by road to Montevideo. Others feature a direct day trip to the capital with a return to Buenos Aires. These differ in travel time, excursion content and the number of nights spent in Uruguay.

Allow time for ferry boarding, border procedures, the journey to the port and sightseeing after arrival. If the visit is limited to one day, a packed schedule may leave little time for museums and independent exploration. History enthusiasts should decide in advance what matters most: a detailed introduction to Buenos Aires, wandering through Colonia's old town or lingering in Montevideo.

Travel documents and border-crossing requirements should be checked for each traveler's citizenship and dates. Ferry schedules and included tickets are likewise determined by the particular itinerary, not by general information about the destination.

## What a journey focused on history and traditions offers

Argentine and Uruguayan cultures developed in the same river region, making it fascinating to observe both common features and local differences. Tango, city cafés and the life of major ports sit alongside the histories of colonial towns and rural traditions. In Argentina, you can discover the world of the gauchos; in Uruguay, the streets of Colonia reveal Portuguese and Spanish heritage.

Adding natural destinations such as Iguazu or Patagonia makes the journey more varied, but reduces the proportion of full days dedicated to cultural sightseeing relative to the total duration. We help compare itineraries by their specific excursions, ferry route and time spent in each city.

## Frequently asked questions about Argentine and Uruguayan culture

### Can you see Uruguay on a day trip from Buenos Aires?

Yes. Some tours include a day excursion by ferry to Montevideo and back to Buenos Aires. It offers an introduction to the capital, not a journey through all of Uruguay's historic towns.

### Which tour visits Colonia del Sacramento?

The [13-day Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) includes a ferry from Buenos Aires to Colonia, a sightseeing visit and the onward journey to Montevideo. On other tours, this stop needs to be checked separately.

### Where can you experience gaucho traditions and tango?

In the Argentine section of several itineraries: Buenos Aires is associated with tango and urban history, while a ranch visit introduces gaucho culture. The [13-day tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/) explicitly includes a day at the Don Silvano ranch.

### How does the 13-day itinerary differ from the 32-day one?

The shorter tour sets aside consecutive days for Buenos Aires, Colonia del Sacramento and Montevideo, followed by relaxation on Uruguay's coast. The longer journey covers eight South American countries and includes only a short Uruguay visit as part of a far broader itinerary.
